clusters.name: Aggression to People and Animals (7 items)

criteria.thresholds: CD: >=3/15 symptoms in 12 months, >=1 in past 6 months (DSM p.530). ASPD: Age >=18, CD onset <15yo, >=3/7 criteria since age 15 (DSM p.748).
subtypes: Childhood-onset type (>=1 symptom <10yo; male predominant, high physical aggression, poorer prognosis) (DSM p.531)
Adolescent-onset type (no symptoms <10yo; balanced sex ratio, better prognosis) (DSM p.531)
Specifier: With limited prosocial emotions / Callous-Unemotional (CU) traits (>=2/4 traits for >=12mo) (DSM p.531)

epidemiology.sex_ratio: CD & ASPD: ~3:1 to 4:1 Male:Female (DSM p.535, p.751).
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: CD: middle childhood to mid-adolescence (rare >16yo) (DSM p.534). ASPD: diagnosis >=18yo with CD <15yo (DSM p.748).
epidemiology.prognosis: ~40% of CD transition to ASPD in adulthood (Dulcan p.211). Burn-out of overt antisocial acts after age 40 (DSM p.750).

etiology.genetic: Low-activity MAO-A genotype + childhood maltreatment increases CD risk 2-fold (Caspi et al.) (Dulcan p.209, p.586).
etiology.neurobiology: Low resting heart rate & low skin conductance (DSM p.535; Dulcan p.210). Impulsive violence 63% due to top-down PFC control deficit (StahlNeuro p.577). VMPFC & OFC NE/DA dysfunction (StahlNeuro p.453, p.487). Reduced amygdala reactivity in CU traits (Dulcan p.210).
etiology.environmental: Hostile attribution bias (DSM p.534; Dulcan p.210). Patterson coercive parenting cycle (Dulcan p.587, p.900). Low verbal IQ (Dulcan p.210). Lead exposure, maternal smoking/substance use (Dulcan p.210, p.589).

first_line: Parent Management Training (PMT / PCIT / Incredible Years) for children <12yo (Dulcan p.204, p.215)
Multisystemic Therapy (MST) 3-5 months home-based for delinquent adolescents (Dulcan p.215, p.1011)
Problem-Solving Skills Training (PSST / CBT) for child (Dulcan p.215)
second_line: Risperidone 0.5-2.5 mg/day for severe physical aggression in CD/ODD (Dulcan p.135, p.214; StahlKids p.470)
Stimulants (Methylphenidate) for comorbid ADHD to reduce impulsive aggression by ~50% (Dulcan p.214, p.597)
Lithium or Valproate for severe refractory aggression (Dulcan p.214, p.597)
key_side_effects: Risperidone: weight gain, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, sedation, EPS (StahlKids p.468, p.472)
treatment.monitoring: Risperidone: BMI monthly for 3 months then quarterly; BP, fasting glucose, lipids baseline, 3 months, then annually (StahlKids p.423, p.471).

items: K-SADS-PL semi-structured diagnostic interview (Dulcan p.42, p.70)
CBCL (Child Behavior Checklist) Externalizing/Aggressive scales (Dulcan p.70, p.202)
OAS / OAS-M (Overt Aggression Scale - Modified) (Dulcan p.213, p.591)
APSD (Antisocial Process Screening Device) for psychopathy/callousness (Dulcan p.213-214)
ICU (Inventory of Callous-Unemotional Traits) 24-item rating scale (Dulcan p.214)
key_numbers: 15 symptoms in CD diagnostic criteria (DSM p.530)
2 of 4 traits required for Callous-Unemotional specifier (DSM p.531)
24 items on Inventory of Callous-Unemotional Traits (ICU) (Dulcan p.214)

items: ADHD (disruptive but no intentional rule/rights violation) (DSM p.536)
ODD (defiance/irritability without physical aggression/property destruction) (DSM p.536)
DMDD (chronic irritability and temper outbursts without criminal/antisocial acts) (DSM p.179, p.536)
IED (unpremeditated impulsive aggressive outbursts without non-aggressive CD rules violations) (DSM p.527-530)
Traumatic Brain Injury / Frontal Lobe Syndrome (Dulcan p.202, p.594)
Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (ictal/interictal aggression) (Dulcan p.594, p.868)
key_numbers: 63% impulsive violence vs 20% psychotic vs 17% psychopathic violence (StahlNeuro p.577)
Age <6 years exclusion for Intermittent Explosive Disorder (DSM p.527)

high_yield: ASPD diagnosis requires age >=18 AND evidence of CD with onset before age 15 (DSM p.748).
CD threshold is >=3 of 15 criteria in past 12 months, with >=1 present in past 6 months (DSM p.530).
Childhood-onset CD (>=1 symptom <10yo) is predominantly male, highly aggressive, and predicts adult ASPD in ~40% of cases (DSM p.531; Dulcan p.211).
Limited prosocial emotions (CU traits) specifier requires >=2 of 4 traits for >=12 months across multiple settings and predicts instrumental aggression (DSM p.531).
Low resting heart rate is the most reliable autonomic physiological marker for CD and antisocial behavior (DSM p.535; Dulcan p.210).
Low-activity MAO-A genotype interacts with childhood abuse to double the risk of CD (Dulcan p.209).
MST (Multisystemic Therapy) is first-line home-based ecological treatment for severely delinquent adolescents (Dulcan p.215, p.1011).
Risperidone is the most evidence-supported drug for severe physical aggression in CD/ODD (Dulcan p.135, p.214; StahlKids p.425).
